raw_response:
I'm 39, been farming these 5 mu since I was 19. My husband works construction in Handan for part of the year, so most days it's me and my mother-in-law in the fields, plus the kids help on weekends when school's out. Five people in the house, but only two and a half of us really farming — that's why I have to watch every yuan.

I've got 2.5 mu in wheat-maize double crop. That's my bread and butter. The wheat went in last October like always — I used improved seed, about 15 kg per mu. For the base fertilizer I put down compound fertilizer, around 25 kg per mu. The extension agent says 20 kg is enough, but Lao Wang next door did 20 and his wheat looked a bit yellow last spring, so I stick with 25. Come March when it greens up, I'll topdress with urea, about 8 kg per mu, and then again at jointing if the leaves look pale — maybe another 8 kg per mu. Water costs keep going up with the meters, so I'll irrigate three times: once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Some folks do four, but that's another 40 yuan in pumping. For pests, I'll spray herbicide once in early spring and watch for aphids.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June — the window's tight, maybe five days if we're lucky. I'll plant hybrid seed, about 3 kg per mu, costs more but you get it back. Base fertilizer goes down at planting, compound fertilizer about 20 kg per mu, then I topdress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 10 kg per mu. Maize needs water at tasseling and filling, so I'll irrigate twice if it's dry. Last year I only did once because the well was being repaired and the yield dropped to maybe 380 kg per mu — won't make that mistake again if I can help it.

Then I've got 1.5 mu in cotton. Cotton is a lot of work, especially picking, but the price was decent last year so I'm keeping it. I plant mid-to-late April. I put phosphate fertilizer as base, about 15 kg per mu of compound, then split urea three times — at planting, at flowering, and at boll stage — total about 12 kg nitrogen per mu. I'll irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage. Can't skip the insecticide for bollworms, and I need herbicide too. I'll probably have to hire a few days of labor for picking in September and October, when the kids are back in school.

The remaining 1 mu is peanuts. I save my own seed, so no seed cost. Peanuts don't need much nitrogen, so I just put down compound fertilizer at planting, about 20 kg per mu, plus some calcium fertilizer my cousin recommended. One irrigation at flowering if it's dry. I spray herbicide after planting and watch for leaf spot — might need fungicide. Peanuts are good because we can eat some at home and sell the rest, and they say it's good for the soil too.

Total input cost this year will be around 2,300 yuan. Fertilizer prices went up again. I could probably push the wheat and maize harder for more yield, but that means buying more urea and paying for more water, and honestly I need to keep some cash in case the well pump breaks or someone gets sick. My husband sends money back, but I don't want to count on that for farm inputs. I'd rather sleep easy knowing I can handle a bad year than squeeze out an extra 50 kg per mu and risk running out of money.
